verdict_note: No compile break and no test failure found by reading. F1 and F2 give wrong answers that no test asserts. Both fixes are a few lines; landing them before the bundled run saves a second build.

findings.what: Run::command_outcome passes `before` to own_op/push, which treat it as a frame count (harness.rs:458 `self.frames.count().saturating_sub(before)`; every other caller passes `self.frames.count()`). Viewer::run_command passes `self.run().ops().len()` instead. Every typed command that reaches no Run op (layout.*, catalog.*, photo.info.*, vector.set_tool_options, vector.add_font, and every pre-dispatch refusal) records observe.frames = frames - ops: 0 or a wrong number, though one frame was emitted.
findings.scenario: A session with 20 frames and 25 ops runs layout.draw_frame: the frame is emitted, but the record says observe.frames 0.
findings.fix: In command_outcome, drop the `before` parameter and take `let before = self.frames.count();` first (the frame is emitted later, inside own_op). Remove the argument at commands.rs:79.

findings.what: For a non-layout typed row, undo_name is the last label of Run::history().undo, whether or not this command added a step. Viewer methods can succeed with no step: develop_change returns Ok on an unchanged edit (view/develop.rs:1024-1026), and set_tiles_and_entry leaves no step on an unchanged entry (harness.rs:1254 keeping_redo_without_new_step). The reply then gives the previous command's step as this command's.
findings.scenario: On a raw document, send photo.develop.kelvin {kelvin:5600} twice: the second reply names the first's step. Or send proof.select working_rgb, then proof.set_proof_colours {on:true} (already on): the reply says 'proof_select'.
findings.fix: Before run_command, read the correlation of the last undo_steps entry; after it, report the last label only if that correlation changed, else null. A count can stay level under a history cap, so do not use the count.

findings.confidence: READ (mechanism); impact on Windows-only builds SUSPECT
findings.what: The size cap trusts metadata().len(). A non-regular file reports 0, then std::fs::read reads until EOF. /dev/zero, /dev/urandom or a FIFO allocates without bound. The size is also checked before the read, so a file that grows in between is not capped.
findings.scenario: vector.add_font {"family":"x","path":"/dev/zero"} on a Unix build: the process is killed for out-of-memory.
findings.fix: Refuse when !meta.is_file() (resource_unreadable). Read with File::open(path)?.take(limit + 1).read_to_end(&mut buf) and refuse resource_too_large when buf.len() > limit.

findings.what: run() opens the Layout Editor panel (toggle_panel creates a fresh LayoutEditor) before edit_of decodes the parameters. A first layout command with an undecodable value is refused, but the panel and editor are left open. The module promises a typed refusal 'before anything runs'.
findings.scenario: layout.draw_frame {page_id:p, x:"NaN", y:0, w:1, h:1} as the session's first layout command: the reply is parameter_invalid, and state.shell.surfaces.layout_editor is now non-null.
findings.fix: Move `let edit = edit_of(id, f)?;` above the editor-open block.

findings.what: A top-level empty JSON array passes the all-strings test vacuously and becomes "". The typed decoders then refuse that "" as parameter_invalid, where the caller meant an empty list. Whether an empty list is valid for each method is not verified.
findings.scenario: design.set_grid_tracks {node:n, rows:[], columns:[{"type":"HUG"}]} is refused parameter_invalid on rows.
findings.fix: Join only non-empty string arrays (`!items.is_empty() && items.iter().all(..)`), so "[]" reaches the decoders. Fields::list already accepts "[]". First check drive_viewer's text_list parsing of "[]".

LayoutEdit::command_id match is exhaustive over all 11 members and their sub-enums. The layout name stacks are pushed, popped, trimmed (MAX_HISTORY) and cleared exactly where the doc stacks are; layout_ui.rs is the only file that touches them, because the fields are private.

Dispatch: 150 typed ids are unique (and unique across all 173 RUN_COMMANDS rows); none equals a viewer canonical id <viewer_domain>.<method> over the 86 DRIVE_VIEWER methods, or one from the doc-new lane's 13 new methods. drive.rs gives timeline./viewer./studio. precedence, and viewer_row_of is filtered by command(id).is_none(). The panel action_of suffixes are unique.

Catalog: timeline keys and spec_commands contain no duplicates and no characters outside the grammar. Tool keys (33) and panel keys (12) are unique snake_case. Menu leaf ids are unique, including proof VIEW and COLOR, which differ (studio.color.proof vs studio.color.proof_menu). Recent leaves are data_label and skipped. No alias equals any author_id.
action_records corpus test: filtered to Surface::Run; command_outcome is a pub &mut fn with its own row. The help sweep in harness_drive.rs is unaffected.

Decoders: line cap 1 MiB, and serde recursion limit 128 at parse_line and again at each f.json re-parse. Mesh 1..=64; shape sides and points are bounded downstream in nib shape::polygon/star; no panicking index or arithmetic in decode.rs.

output_path guards: every typed row that writes a file (export_svg/pdf path, import_vector dest, batch_add output) declares OUTPUT_PATH and an overwrite flag. The guard matches the viewer-row export guard (same_file, then exists without overwrite). source follows import_vector dest only on success.
Attribution: every drive command requires --actor and --session (package_of). Typed rows run under the viewer's RunContext, and layout-only rows are recorded through command_outcome with that actor.
